item.title: Trump pauses all asylum decisions; order follows shooting near White House
item.description: The Trump administration has ordered USCIS officers to halt all asylum decisions following an attack by an Afghan asylum recipient. This directive, affecting all nationalities, instructs officers to pause approvals, denials, and case closures until further notice. The move aims to enhance vetting processes and prioritize public safety amid broader immigration actions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Treated very harshly': Trump pardons ex-Honduras president Hernandez ahead of elections
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump has pardoned Honduras' ex-leader Juan Orlando Hernandez, convicted of drug trafficking. Trump's move, just before Honduras' presidential election, comes with a stark warning: US aid hinges on his preferred candidate, Nasry Asfura, winning. Trump claims Hernandez was treated unfairly, while accusing other candidates of being communist or spoilers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: DC shooting: US Treasury to cut federal benefits to 'illegal aliens' amid Trump’s rant on immigrants from third-world countries
item.description: In a sweeping policy shift, the US Treasury has announced plans to limit federal tax benefits for undocumented immigrants, reflecting President Trump's directive to prioritize American citizens. This decision comes in the aftermath of a tragic incident involving an Afghan national, which has reignited discussions on immigration from 'Third World countries.

item.title: Donald Trump claims any document signed by Joe Biden using autopen is 'terminated', warns former prez could face ‘charges of perjury’
item.description: In a dramatic turn of events, ex-President Donald Trump has announced the invalidation of executive orders issued by Joe Biden via autopen, alleging misuse of the device. Trump has also issued a stern warning of potential perjury accusations against Biden if he maintains that his staff acted under his orders.

item.title: 'Stop sending millions of dollars to...': Ex-Afghanistan VP makes 3 requests to Trump govt after DC shooting
item.description: Former Afghanistan Vice President Amrullah Saleh called out the Donald Trump administration for sending millions of dollars to the Taliban government every week when it's acting all tough on Afghans after DC shooter was identified as Rahmanullah Lakanwal. Calling Lakanwal the worst Afghan, Amrullah Saleh said 40 million Afghans should not pay the price of what Lakanwa did.

item.title: Man tells Ontario court he did 'sham marriages' in India to help Indian women immigrate to Canada
item.description: An Indian-origin man confessed in an Ontario court to participating in two sham marriages to aid Indian women in immigrating to Canada. In exchange for cash and care for his mother, Amratpal Singh Sidhu admitted to the deceit. The court, hearing a case between Sidhu and his first wife Amandeep Kaur, declared their marriage invalid due to these revelations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Russian Popeye’: Man who injected Vaseline oil for giant biceps now faces possible arm amputation
item.description: Kirill Tereshin, known as the “Russian Popeye,” spent years injecting petroleum jelly into his arms in pursuit of exaggerated biceps and online attention. Now, facing severe tissue damage and infection, doctors warn he may lose both arms without urgent reconstructive treatment. His case has shifted from spectacle to medical crisis, exposing the real human costs behind extreme body modification and social-media-driven obsession.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Perez Hilton reacts as Meghan Markle is accused of keeping $1,700 green gown from a photoshoot without asking
item.description: A resurfaced rumor about Meghan Markle taking a designer gown without permission, dubbed "Green Gown-gate," has sparked debate. Podcaster Perez Hilton defended Meghan, calling the claims "nonsense." Meanwhile, Meghan and Prince Harry actively participated in a Thanksgiving meal packing event through their Archewell Foundation, offering a positive counterpoint to the dress controversy.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Ukraine corruption crisis: Zelenskyy’s chief of staff Andrii Yermak resigns after raid
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy accepted the resignation of his chief of staff, Andrii Yermak, following searches of his residence by anti-corruption investigators. The move comes amid intense US pressure for a settlement and a major corruption probe, with Yermak cooperating fully and not yet formally accused.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Candace Owens reacts after woman says TPUSA Faith event speaker called her evil and blasted Tucker Carlson
item.description: Candace Owens has slammed a Turning Point USA "Faith" event speaker who allegedly insulted her and Tucker Carlson. Owens praised young attendees for identifying "fake pastors," stating Charlie Kirk wouldn't permit such "naked propaganda." Separately, Owens announced her show is off-air due to safety fears, making a serious claim about French President Macron attempting to have her killed.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: 'Had mental problems from what he saw in Afghanistan': Childhood friend says DC shooter Rahmanullah Lakanwal could not tolerate blood
item.description: A childhood friend of Lakanwal’s told New York Times that the shooting suspect suffered mental problems from what he saw in Afghanistan. “When he saw blood, bodies, and the wounded, he could not tolerate it,” the friend told the New York Times. “It put a lot of pressure on his mind.”

item.title: Which river crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice: The unique journey and geography of the Limpopo River
item.description: Africa's Limpopo River, an S-shaped wonder, uniquely crosses the Tropic of Capricorn twice. This vital transboundary waterway, spanning four nations, shapes borders, supports diverse ecosystems, and has a rich history, including ancient trading kingdoms. Its seasonal flow and wildlife make it a crucial lifeline for southern Africa's people and biodiversity.
